summary: Classify each V1-pinned test and produce a concrete V2 migration verdict

verdicts.v1_mechanism: Concurrent chaos stress of the V1 stale-state/invalidation model. Three V1-only primitives: (1) direct plain-BTC self-split via wallet.split_coin(id, piece) for DAG-deepening (split action L582, respend-split L628); (2) V1 decrementing-locktime backup-tx clawback cheats — capture the latest backup via sqlite_manager::get_backup_txs then broadcast that stale non-final backup to try to claw a coin back after send (steal_after_send) or after split (steal_after_split, which itself calls split_coin at cheats.rs:175); (3) an oracle whose stuck-coin ('off-chain sub-coin with NO backup AND no exit path') and branch-depth (max backup-row count) invariants are keyed on the V1 backup-tx chain. Pinned V1 at line 236 (UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT=1).
verdicts.v2_analogue: in_ladder_pay (clients/libs/rust-sdk/src/transfer.rs:625) is the B1-safe replacement for split_coin; transfer() already auto-routes laddered coins to it (transfer.rs:133-142) and transfer_sender::execute conveys Model-A S' for whole-coin V2 sends (transfer_sender.rs:301-325). The V2 anti-theft mechanism (TES-R CSV ladder + terminal-freeze + verify_bundle anti-theft count) replaces the V1 backup-tx clawback and is exercised single-threaded by sdk50 (V2 unilateral_exit), sdk54 + sdk55 (verify_bundle / backup-chain adversarial: padding, inversion, hidden low-CSV state), and sdk58 (in-ladder split child accept). BUT there is NO V2 concurrent/chaos multi-user test — chaos22 is the only one — so the concurrent property is not covered elsewhere.
verdicts.migration_plan: Remove the pin (delete line 236 so it runs on the V2 default). Swap the three split_coin(id, piece) call sites to the V2 in-ladder split: wallet.in_ladder_pay(&id, recipient_addr, piece, InLadderLatch::None) — for the self-split split/respend actions pass a peer address (or me.address) and treat the returned piece_child as a conveyed child the recipient claim()s, matching V2 payment semantics; the change child stays local/exitable. Rewrite the steal_after_split cheat to the V2 clawback vector: after in_ladder_pay terminalizes the parent, attempt to broadcast a SUPERSEDED ladder tier / hidden lower-CSV state (the sdk54/sdk55 attack shape) instead of a V1 backup, keeping the same chaos_fault emit shape (o_txid/o_vout/stale_txid) so the oracle's on-chain fraud backstop (funding outpoint never spent by the stale tx) still applies unchanged. steal_after_send can keep the whole-coin send leg (works on V2) but its clawback should likewise broadcast the retained superseded state rather than only the V1 backup. In the oracle, keep the value-conservation (Sum SE <= D), double-custody, and outpoint-single-spender invariants as-is (protocol-agnostic); re-express the stuck-coin / branch-depth checks in TES-R terms — replace 'no backup + no exit path' with estimate_exit_cost/tesr::load presence, since V2 exitability is the ladder, not the backup chain (note sdk55: V2 still conveys V1 backups, so get_backup_txs is not empty and the current stuck heuristic would misfire). Do NOT whitelist the B1 'has a V2 exit ladder and cannot be split' message as contention in classify() (that would mask a real regression). Retiring is NOT valid here: no V2 test covers no-value-created / no-cheat-succeeds / no-double-custody / liveness under CONCURRENCY.
verdicts.risk: The concurrent anti-theft guarantee must be preserved end-to-end: no stale/superseded prior-owner state (V2: an old trigger/extension/state or a hidden lower-CSV Model-A state) may ever claw a coin back — verified on-chain that each coin's funding outpoint is never spent by the cheater's stale tx (INV-5/18/19) — together with no value created (Sum SE-side balances <= total deposited D), single custody per statechain_id (no double-spend), and liveness/bounded-contention, all under many concurrent users. The rewrite must keep an ACTUAL adversarial cheat exercising the V2 clawback vector; merely deleting the V1 backup-broadcast cheat would silently drop the security property this test exists to prove.

verdicts.v1_mechanism: Case 2's direct `alice.split_coin(&parent_id, 15_000)` call (clients/libs/rust-sdk/src/transfer.rs:467): the V1 plain-BTC off-chain self-split of a confirmed coin into two wallet-owned piece+change sub-coins, with the parent made terminal via set_spend_budget=1. The test asserts the surviving property that after the split the parent is terminally spent (re-spend of the full parent value refused) while piece+change stay usable. Under V2 this exact call is refused by the B1 guard (transfer.rs:502-509) because a fresh SDK deposit auto-establishes a TES-R ladder at claim() (wallet.rs:458, UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT defaults to 2 in config.rs:84). Cases 1 (typed InsufficientBalance), 3 (claim idempotence) and 4 (double-withdraw refusal) are NOT V1-specific — they are SDK guard-rails that also hold on V2.
verdicts.v2_analogue: in_ladder_pay (clients/libs/rust-sdk/src/transfer.rs:625) is the B1-safe replacement for split_coin; transfer() auto-routes a non-exact spend of a laddered coin to it (transfer.rs:133-146); withdraw() already routes a received in-ladder child claim to unilateral_exit (wallet.rs:846-863). Existing V2 tests: sdk58_inladder_split (asserts parent+child TERMINAL after the split, plus 10 adversarial verify_child_bundle attacks incl. value-spoof) and sdk59_inladder_pay (transfer -> in-ladder split -> Bob claim/adopt -> Bob unilateral_exit). NOTE: neither sdk58 nor sdk59 covers sdk04's four SDK-API guard-rails (typed InsufficientBalance, SDK-level split-parent re-spend refusal, claim idempotence no-double-book, double-withdraw refusal), so those are NOT already covered elsewhere.
verdicts.migration_plan: 1) Delete the V1 pin at line 31 (`std::env::set_var("UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT","1")`) and the stale V1-LANE comment (lines 28-30); the wallets then run V2-native and claim() auto-ladders alice's 40k coin. 2) Case 1 (lines 57-60) passes unchanged — transfer() returns SdkError::InsufficientBalance on any protocol. 3) Case 2 (lines 62-88): replace the direct `split_coin(&parent_id, 15_000)` with the V2 in-ladder path — either `alice.in_ladder_pay(&parent_id, &bob_address, 15_000, InLadderLatch::None)` (import mercury_utexo_sdk::InLadderLatch) or `alice.transfer(&bob_address, 15_000)` asserting `r.used_split`. This ALSO subsumes line 86's separate piece-transfer (the piece is conveyed directly to Bob inside the split), so drop lines 85-88's `alice.transfer(bob,15_000)`. Rewrite the double-spend assertion (lines 78-83): keep `alice.transfer(&bob_address, 40_000).await.unwrap_err()` (now fails as InsufficientBalance — parent WITHDRAWN, only change left) AND add a FAITHFUL re-spend refusal: `alice.in_ladder_pay(&parent_id, &bob_address, 5_000, InLadderLatch::None).await.unwrap_err()` must fail because the parent is terminal at the SE (budget=1 consumed by SP, per sdk58's parent_terminal assert). 4) Case 3 (lines 90-98): keep the claim-idempotence assertions but wrap the first `bob.claim()` in a short wait-loop (as sdk59 does) since the piece arrives via mailbox conveyance, not a synchronous exact handover; assert first pass claimed_transfers==1 then ==0, balance==15_000 once. 5) Case 4 (lines 100-109): Bob now holds an exit-only child claim, so `bob.withdraw(&exit_addr, None, None)` routes it to unilateral_exit + marks WITHDRAWING (wallet.rs:846-863) and the value lands at BOB's own key (not exit_addr) — adjust that expectation, and re-assert the double-withdraw refusal against the WITHDRAWING/already-exiting child. Alternatively, to preserve the ORIGINAL cooperative-withdraw double-spend property verbatim, give Bob a normal V2 coin (an exact-amount transfer or his own deposit) so withdraw goes through withdraw::execute and the SE-level double-withdraw refusal holds as in V1. No new capability is required — every path (in_ladder_pay, transfer auto-route, child-claim withdraw) already exists.
verdicts.risk: The load-bearing assertion is the split-parent DOUBLE-SPEND refusal: after splitting, the parent must be unspendable and cannot yield a second payment. Under V2 this becomes "the parent is terminal at the SE (spend budget consumed by SP) so a second in_ladder_pay/transfer of the parent sid is refused." This SDK-API-level refusal is NOT redundantly covered — sdk58 only asserts the verifier-side terminal flag, not that a re-spend call through the wallet is rejected — so the rewrite MUST keep an explicit re-spend-refusal assertion; do not drop it to InsufficientBalance alone. Also preserve the other three guard-rails (typed InsufficientBalance, claim idempotence / no double-booking, double-withdraw refusal), none of which any other V2 test covers. Because these properties are unique to this test, retiring it (obsolete-retire) is INVALID — it would silently drop four security assertions.

verdicts.v1_mechanism: Part B only: V1 branch-model / single_use sub-coins via split_coin (transfer.rs:467) + the verify_terminal_parents receiver guard (transfer_receiver.rs:496-560) that a 20k-from-60k transfer triggers. Parts C (MuSig2 secnonce single-use / SE key-share leak) and D (/transfer/unlock auth bypass + 500 panic) are NOT V1-specific — they are SE/lockbox-level properties keyed on the sealed secnonce and statechain_id, identical under V1 and V2.
verdicts.v2_analogue: Part B: in_ladder_pay (transfer.rs:625) + verify_child_bundle census replace the branch model; the surviving honest-split-payment property is already covered by sdk59_inladder_pay (bob.get_balance()==PAY). Parts C and D: NONE — protocol-agnostic security guards (lockbox/src/enclave.cpp + server/src/endpoints/sign.rs; server/src/endpoints/transfer_receiver.rs), uniquely tested here; must be preserved, not retired.
verdicts.migration_plan: 1) Remove the pin (delete set_var("UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT","1"), or set cfg.deposit_protocol_version=2) so alice's 60k deposit is laddered. 2) Part B: alice.transfer(&bob,20_000) now auto-routes to in_ladder_pay (transfer.rs:141-143). Keep the value assertion bob.get_balance().available_sats==20_000 (holds per sdk59); replace bob.claim().claimed_transfers==1 with the sdk59 balance-poll pattern (an in-ladder child adoption may not increment claimed_transfers). REWRITE the assertion messages: the terminal_parents/branch semantics do not exist on V2 (receiver uses verify_child_bundle census). Since sdk59 already covers the honest-payment property, Part B degrades to a value-flow smoke check — do NOT keep it as a terminal_parents test. 3) Part C (CRITICAL, preserve verbatim): bob's in-ladder child has no SE key (transfer.rs:60-64), so re-point `victim` to a coin with a live 2-of-2 and finalized==0 — e.g. bob makes his own fresh V2 deposit, or alice sends bob a WHOLE coin via an exact-amount transfer (V2 exact = key handover via transfer_sender::execute). The raw flow (create_and_commit_nonces -> transaction::sign_first -> get_partial_sig_request to addr_c then addr_d -> transaction::sign_second) and both assertions (sig_c.is_ok(), sig_d.is_err()) stay UNCHANGED. 4) Part D: use that same coin's statechain_id for the real-id case; the unknown-id case and both 403 assertions stay verbatim (endpoint is protocol-agnostic).
verdicts.risk: Two SE security assertions with NO V2 equivalent test MUST survive the migration: (1) MuSig2 secnonce single-use — a 2nd /sign/second reusing one server nonce over a different message must be refused, else SE key-share extraction yields two co-signed conflicting spends of one coin while the finalized counter reads 1 (defeats single_use/budget/epoch and the whole 2-of-2); (2) /transfer/unlock with a bad sig + null auth_pub_key must return 403 (no auth bypass) and must not 500-panic on an unknown statechain_id. Do not let the Part C victim re-point silently disable the probe (verify sig_c actually co-signs before sig_d is attempted).

verdicts.v1_mechanism: V1 decrementing-ABSOLUTE-locktime stale state: a prior owner (alice) retains the parent's pre-signed deposit backup (a valid tx spending funding outpoint F/O with a HIGH nLockTime), captured via get_backup_txs + mercurylib::utils::get_blockheight. The defense is split_coin's locktime-FREE branch sub-coin (backup key `branch-{piece_id}`) winning the locktime race, and a fallback on-chain watcher (SafeOffchain/SafeExited/Fraud). Scenario 2 tests the V1-only RISK that the stale backup becomes FINAL and the attacker wins if the receiver is offline past the absolute-locktime deadline — the "backup floors/becomes final after the deadline" premise TES-R's idle-coins-never-age directly contradicts.
verdicts.v2_analogue: sdk51_v2_watchtower
verdicts.migration_plan: RETIRE (delete clients/tests/rust/src/sdk13_stale_state.rs; drop `pub mod sdk13_stale_state;` at main.rs:35 and the `sdk13_stale_state::execute()` dispatch at main.rs:133). Do NOT merely remove the UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT="1" pin: the test's entire subject is a V1 absolute-nLockTime construct that does not exist under TES-R. Under V2, transfer() routes the laddered coin through in_ladder_pay (a STATE tier descending from the trigger, Model A) rather than split_coin, so capture_stale (reads the single absolute-locktime deposit backup) and branch_root_txid (reads the `branch-{piece_id}` V1 branch) would find nothing, and Scenario 2 (mine past the absolute locktime so the stale backup becomes final and the attacker wins) has no V2 counterpart because idle coins never age and the owner's lowest-CSV state always wins the race. Every surviving security assertion is ALREADY covered by a dedicated V2 test: [A] pre-maturity non-final broadcast -> tiers only broadcast at CSV maturity (sdk50/sdk45/sdk51); [B]+[D] honest exit spends F and watcher sees SafeExited -> sdk50/sdk51 land funds at the owner; [C] double-spend-after-O-spent + the load-bearing "a prior owner cannot claw back a coin they already split" -> sdk58 attack H (terminality) + sdk51 (owner wins the CSV race); SafeOffchain idle verdict -> sdk51 step-1 defend_ladders no-op. Retirement justification: the surviving property (prior-owner stale-state claw-back defeat + watchtower defense) is fully covered by sdk51 + sdk45 + sdk58, so retiring drops no untested security property. Optional hardening (not a blocker): add one negative assertion in sdk51 that the on-chain spender of F equals the owner's own exit tier (the explicit anti-Fraud check), documenting that under V2 the fraud outcome is PREVENTED, not merely detected. Confirm sdk45/sdk51/sdk58 are green before deleting.
verdicts.risk: A prior owner must never be able to claw back / double-spend the funding outpoint F of a coin they already transferred or split, and the honest current owner's exit must always win the race. Under V2 this is preserved by (a) the current owner's adopted state carrying the strictly-lowest CSV (sdk51, and the R-prime re-anchor sdk46/47) and (b) parent terminality after an in-ladder split so no rival trigger over F can be co-signed (sdk58 attack H). Do not delete sdk13 without first confirming sdk45, sdk51, and sdk58 are green — retiring the absolute-locktime lane must not silently drop the "prior owner cannot steal via a retained state over F" guarantee.

verdicts.v1_mechanism: The V1 decrementing-ABSOLUTE-locktime stale-state invalidation model. Concretely: (1) `capture_stale` reads the parent deposit backup via `get_backup_txs` + `get_blockheight` to get an absolute locktime L_old — the "stale state" a paying prior owner retains; (2) `alice.transfer(bob,15k)` with `assert!(r.used_split)` on a V1-pinned coin routes through `split_coin` (transfer.rs:148) producing a locktime-FREE branch sub-coin for Bob (NOT in_ladder_pay); (3) the watchtower premise "deadline = stale backup locktime": inside [now, L_old) the attacker's absolute-locktime backup is non-final so cannot be broadcast, making the receiver's branch exit uncontested; (4) after `bob.unilateral_exit` spends F, the test broadcasts `stale.backup_hex` past the deadline and asserts it is REJECTED (input already spent). Every load-bearing element (absolute-locktime deposit backup that a prior owner can re-broadcast, a coin-aging "deadline", the locktime-free V1 branch from split_coin) is V1-only.
verdicts.v2_analogue: sdk51_v2_watchtower (primary: prior-owner-races-stale-state -> owner defend_ladders() -> lowest-CSV current state matures first and wins; also proves idle V2 coin never ages) + sdk40_tesr_consensus PART 2 (stale ladder defeated at consensus level, prevout gone) + sdk50_v2_unilateral_exit (honest unilateral exit via ladder, no V1 absolute-locktime backup) + sdk45_tesr_watchtower (keyless/offline-owner watchtower) + sdk58_inladder_split attacks H/I (rival trigger over F / rival state over SP.out[j] rejected). Underlying V2 machinery: wallet.rs defend_ladders()/tesr::watch_pass (763-801).
verdicts.migration_plan: RETIRE. Delete clients/tests/rust/src/sdk14_watcher_race.rs; remove `pub mod sdk14_watcher_race;` (main.rs:36) and the dispatch arm `sdk14_watcher_race::execute().await?;` (main.rs:137). No code path depends on it (only a doc-comment reference in sdk15_fresh_doublesign.rs:2 mentions "sdk13/sdk14" — leave or reword; not load-bearing). Retirement is justified because the V1 mechanism it tests is structurally gone under TES-R: idle coins never age so there is no "deadline"; there is no absolute-locktime deposit backup for a prior owner to re-broadcast; a contested exit is resolved by CSV maturity order, not a locktime non-final window. Every surviving security property is already covered on V2 with STRONGER guarantees: the contested-exit-owner-wins race = sdk51 (verified on live SE, driven purely by defend_ladders()); the stale-state-cannot-confirm double-spend property = sdk40 PART 2 ("old state dies at the consensus level"); honest unilateral exit = sdk50; offline/keyless watchtower liveness = sdk45; the clawback vectors (rival trigger over F, rival over the descendant tier) = sdk58 attacks H and I. Do NOT rewrite onto V2 — a rewrite would only duplicate sdk40+sdk50+sdk51; there is no residual sdk14 property left uncovered. Precondition for the deletion: sdk40, sdk50, sdk51, sdk45, sdk58 must remain in the suite (they hold the assertion sdk14 was guarding).
verdicts.risk: A stale/prior-owner state must NEVER claw back a coin whose funding F the honest current owner's state has already spent, and an honest receiver of an off-chain (split/ladder) payment must always be able to unilaterally exit and win a contested exit before losing the funds. This is preserved on V2 by sdk51 (lowest-CSV current state wins the race) + sdk40 PART 2 (stale ladder can never confirm once its prevout is spent) + sdk50 (unilateral exit) + sdk58 H/I (rival co-signs rejected). Retiring sdk14 is only safe while those tests exist; deleting any of them without a replacement would silently drop this clawback-defense assertion.

verdicts.v1_mechanism: The V1 decrementing-locktime backup-tx path, `mercuryrustlib::transaction::new_transaction(&cc, &mut c, addr, ..., si.initlock, si.interval)` (clients/libs/rust/src/transaction.rs:9), called TWICE on cloned coin state to obtain two conflicting FRESH SE co-signatures of the same funding outpoint. Each call runs sign_first + sign_second (fresh nonce) and packages a V1 absolute-locktime backup. Premise: a NORMAL coin (single_use=false, no budget) for which the honest SE re-signs freely — "exactly the code path a single-use-ignoring SE would take." What it PROVES is protocol-independent: a fresh co-sign carries a current locktime, so the decrementing-locktime ladder gives NO advantage — it degrades to a plain first-seen/highest-fee on-chain race. This is the irreducible single-SE trust floor.
verdicts.v2_analogue: Co-sign path exists but NO covering V2 test. Path: `tesr::establish`/`establish_auto` (clients/libs/rust/src/tesr.rs:141/187) drives the shared blind-MuSig2 co-sign `tesr::cosign_tier` (tesr.rs:1518, pub) over the LOCKTIME-FREE trigger tier from `mercurylib::tesr::build_trigger(f_txid, f_vout, ...)`; the trigger spends the same funding outpoint F — the exact V2 analogue of the V1 backup spend. TRUST-MODEL.md §8 line 341 maps "Fresh double-sign trust floor" ONLY to sdk15. sdk12 (line 340) is the OPPOSITE property (nonce-atomicity: SE CANNOT double-sign behind the receiver's back); sdk54/sdk55 attack verify_bundle count-padding, not the fresh-co-sign race. So the analogue is a code path, not a covering test — this rules out obsolete-retire.
verdicts.migration_plan: 1) Remove the pin: delete `std::env::set_var("UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT","1")` (line 30) + its V1DEF-5 comment. 2) Deposit a V2 coin on the default path (reuse sdk40 `deposit_coin`, or keep the existing add_prepaid_token + get_deposit_address(40_000) + claim loop — under V2 default this yields a laddered coin). 3) SWAP the two `transaction::new_transaction(&cc,&mut c1/c2,addr_x/addr_y,...)` calls for two conflicting V2 trigger co-signs of the same F: on `c1=coin.clone()` do `let t=mercurylib::tesr::build_trigger(f_txid,f_vout,f_value,agg,"regtest",2.0)?` then `tesr::cosign_tier(&cc,&mut c1,t.tx_hex,f_value,"regtest").await?` -> tx_X; repeat on `c2=coin.clone()` (fresh nonce; vary fee_rate/exit so the triggers differ) -> tx_Y. Both triggers spend F, so they conflict. (Two `establish_auto` calls on clones with distinct owner_exit addresses is an equivalent higher-level driver.) 4) KEEP the three assertions in force: `txx.input[0].previous_output==txy.input[0].previous_output` (same F), tx_X broadcast is_ok, tx_Y broadcast is_err after tx_X confirms (already-spent). 5) REWRITE the doc-comment + final println: "decrementing-locktime ladder gives no advantage" -> "the V2 CSV tier chain gives no advantage — the trigger is locktime-free, so two conflicting fresh triggers over F are a first-seen race"; keep the "closed only by threshold-signing the SE" conclusion. 6) Model the willing SE: if the honest V2 SE's budget-monotonicity guard (set_spend_budget min(), lockbox secnonce one-shot; TRUST-MODEL B10/B1) refuses the second trigger co-sign, deposit a coin with budget headroom or drive `cosign_tier` on the cloned state directly — the same "re-sign a normal coin = what an ignoring SE does" trick the V1 test already uses. 7) Keep TRUST-MODEL.md §8:341 pointing at sdk15.
verdicts.risk: Preserve the irreducible single-SE fresh-double-sign trust floor (T-SE-1): a single WILLING SE (or SE + old-owner collusion) can produce two conflicting FRESH co-signatures of the same funding outpoint, and no client-side layer — ladder (V1 locktime OR V2 CSV), single_use, terminal/budget query — closes it; only threshold-signing does; resolution is a first-seen/highest-fee race the honest owner wins by fee-bump head start. sdk15 is the SOLE test documenting this (TRUST-MODEL.md §8:341). Must NOT be retired or downgraded: the same-outpoint + first-seen-race assertions and the "no ladder/CSV advantage vs a fresh co-sign" conclusion must survive the port to the V2 trigger path, and must not be conflated with sdk12's inverse nonce-atomicity guarantee.

verdicts.v1_mechanism: Multi-hop OFF-CHAIN re-transfer of a RECEIVED split sub-coin. sdk17 chains alice->bob->carol where each hop is a non-exact (split) payment and the funding outpoint O stays unspent through both hops. The load-bearing V1-only step is hop 2: bob RE-SPENDS the 20k sub-coin he received from alice's split, sending 10k to carol off-chain (`bob.transfer(&carol_addr, 10_000)` with `assert!(r2.used_split)`). On the V1 lane a received split piece is a first-class statechain coin (the key-handover conveyed the full SE co-signing relationship), so bob can re-transfer it off-chain with zero on-chain footprint. This is the Ark/Arkade out-of-round + Spark leaf-transfer chaining property.
verdicts.v2_analogue: sdk59_inladder_pay — covers ONLY the single hop (alice pays bob a non-exact amount via in_ladder_pay, bob adopts the ctesr child via verify_child_bundle, bob unilateral_exits, funds land at bob's key, O unspent until exit). It does NOT cover bob re-transferring the received child. No V2 test does an A->B->C off-chain chain. So the surviving single-hop OOR property is already covered; the multi-hop re-transfer is the uncovered gap.
verdicts.migration_plan: CANNOT pass-as-is: removing the `UTEXO_PROTOCOL_DEFAULT="1"` pin (line 48) makes hop 1 pass (in_ladder_pay auto-route, used_split=true, bob balance==20k, O unspent — matches sdk59), but hop 2 FAILS: bob's received 20k is an in-ladder split CHILD CLAIM (persisted `ctesr-<id>` bundle, adopted via load_child), which `transfer()` excludes from spendable selection (clients/libs/rust-sdk/src/transfer.rs:65-82 via tesr::child_claim_sids, tesr.rs:425-437) because it is exit-only (no SE co-signing key; funding SP.out[j] is un-broadcast). So `bob.transfer(&carol_addr,10_000)` returns InsufficientBalance. This is the UN-FIXED v2-child-retransfer-unsound gap. FEATURE TO BUILD FIRST: off-chain re-transfer of a received in-ladder split child = the v2-child-retransfer-unsound FIXED design (full key-handover of the conveyed child + terminalize + reopen BOUND TO the conveyance recipient + N-hop census in the SSP verify_bundle pre-pay so a prior owner cannot broadcast a competing branch). AFTER the feature lands: (1) remove the line-48 pin; (2) allow the received child sid into hop-2 selection (stop excluding it, or route through a new re-convey path) so `bob.transfer(&carol,10_000)` re-conveys and carol's claim() adopts the grand-child; (3) rewrite the final exit (lines 107-110) from the V1 one-block assumption to the V2 multi-step CSV-tier loop as sdk59 does (loop `carol.unilateral_exit(...)`; on `!complete` generate `s.wait_blocks.max(1)+1` blocks; stop on complete), then assert `is_outpoint_spent(O)` and that child_value lands at carol's own key. The used_split, off-chain-balance, and "O unspent through both hops" assertions are preserved as-is (they hold once re-transfer exists).
verdicts.gap_detail: V2 (TES-R) cannot re-transfer a RECEIVED in-ladder split child off-chain. Received children are `ctesr-` bundles that are exit-only (exit_child_pass / unilateral_exit) and are deliberately excluded from transfer() spend selection because their off-chain re-transfer is not soundly verifiable (v2-child-retransfer-unsound, UN-FIXED / under design re-verification). To support the multi-hop OOR chain the protocol must add: sound child re-transfer = full key-handover of the conveyed child, terminalize the child, bind any reopen to the conveyance recipient (not a prior owner), and an N-hop census in the SSP pre-pay verify_bundle. This is a real protocol capability, not a test rewrite: no existing V2 path lets a received split piece be re-spent off-chain.
verdicts.risk: The OOR re-transfer must NOT let a prior owner steal the value. Under the naive design, bob (or alice) re-opening/self-reopening the branch after conveying it to carol = theft (v2-child-retransfer-unsound), and splitting a laddered coin whose prior owner holds a no-timelock trigger is exactly the B1 void-the-split attack. The ported feature MUST bind reopen to the conveyance recipient and run the N-hop census in the SSP pre-pay so a prior owner cannot broadcast a competing branch. Also preserve the two invariants sdk17 asserts: (a) funding outpoint O stays UNSPENT through every off-chain hop and is spent ONLY by the final unilateral exit, and (b) the exited value lands at the LAST recipient's own key. Do not enable child re-transfer without the recipient-bound reopen + census, or the split-child theft vector is reintroduced.

## 2. GENUINE FEATURE GAPS

Exactly **one** test carries `genuine_feature_gap=true`:

**sdk17_oor_chain** — multi-hop off-chain re-transfer of a *received* in-ladder split child. Under V2, a received child is a `ctesr-<id>` bundle that is **exit-only** (no SE co-signing key; funding `SP.out[j]` un-broadcast) and is deliberately excluded from `transfer()` spend selection (`transfer.rs:65-82` via `tesr::child_claim_sids`), so hop 2 (`bob.transfer(carol, 10_000)`) returns `InsufficientBalance`. This is the still-open `v2-child-retransfer-unsound` item.

Must be built before sdk17 can migrate:
- Full key-handover of the conveyed child (turn the exit-only child into a first-class re-transferable coin).
- Terminalize the child on re-conveyance.
- **Bind reopen to the conveyance recipient**, not to any prior owner (this is the anti-theft crux — naive self-reopen by bob/alice = theft).
- N-hop census in the SSP pre-pay `verify_bundle` so a prior owner cannot broadcast a competing branch.

This is the sole real protocol capability on the list. Its soundness is still under re-verification per the memory note; do **not** enable child re-transfer without the recipient-bound reopen + census, or the split-child theft vector (and the B1 void-the-split attack) is reintroduced. Everything else — including every "colored in-ladder split" surface — is test migration, not new capability. The colored-in-ladder-split blocker was indeed a misdiagnosis for all buckets except this one.

## 4. Risks — assertions that must survive each migration

**Concurrency anti-theft (chaos22).** No stale/superseded prior-owner state (old trigger/extension/state or a hidden lower-CSV Model-A state) may ever claw a coin back, verified on-chain that each coin's funding outpoint is never spent by the cheater's stale tx (INV-5/18/19), together with no value created (Σ SE-side ≤ D), single custody per `statechain_id`, and bounded-contention liveness — **all under many concurrent users**. The rewrite must keep a live adversarial cheat exercising the V2 clawback vector; merely deleting the V1 backup-broadcast cheat silently drops the property.

**Split-parent double-spend refusal (sdk04).** After an in-ladder split the parent must be terminal at the SE (spend budget consumed) so a second `in_ladder_pay`/`transfer` of the parent sid is refused at the wallet API. sdk58 only asserts the verifier-side flag — keep an explicit re-spend-refusal call, do not degrade to `InsufficientBalance` alone. Also preserve typed InsufficientBalance, claim idempotence, and double-withdraw refusal (none covered elsewhere).

**SE secnonce single-use + unlock auth (sdk12).** A 2nd `/sign/second` reusing one server nonce over a different message must be refused (else SE key-share extraction yields two co-signed conflicting spends while `finalized`==1). `/transfer/unlock` with bad sig + null `auth_pub_key` must return 403 and not 500-panic on unknown id. Verify the re-pointed Part C victim actually co-signs (`sig_c.is_ok()`) before `sig_d` is attempted, or the probe silently disables itself.

**Fresh double-sign trust floor (sdk15).** The irreducible T-SE-1: a willing SE (or SE+old-owner) can produce two conflicting fresh co-signs of the same funding outpoint, and no client layer (V1 locktime or V2 CSV, single_use, terminal/budget query) closes it — only threshold-signing does; resolution is a first-seen/fee race the honest owner wins by fee-bump head start. Same-outpoint + first-seen-race asserts and the "no CSV advantage vs a fresh co-sign" conclusion must port to the trigger path. Must not be conflated with sdk12's inverse nonce-atomicity guarantee. Sole documentation at TRUST-MODEL.md §8:341.

**OOR re-transfer theft (sdk17).** Reopen must be bound to the conveyance recipient, with the N-hop census in the SSP pre-pay, so a prior owner cannot broadcast a competing branch (self-reopen = theft; splitting a laddered coin whose prior owner holds a no-timelock trigger = the B1 void-the-split attack). Preserve: (a) funding outpoint O stays unspent through every off-chain hop, spent only by the final unilateral exit; (b) exited value lands at the last recipient's own key.

**Receive fund-safety (sdk19, sdk24, sdk25).** With no LN payment: SE must not reveal the preimage (`retrieve_pre_image.is_err`), receiver cannot claim (balance 0), HODL invoice never `Succeeded`, SSP's fronted coin stays fully recoverable. sdk24 adds payer HTLC fails-back on abort; sdk25 adds the [2]/[5] two-clock atomicity (a delayed receiver past the SE latch window gets nothing, payer refunded). None are covered by any V2 test — these may only be re-pointed, never retired. Keep the SE-latch-wiring precheck so a withheld preimage is attributable to non-payment, not a broken batch.

**Pay-failure recovery (sdk18 retire).** Preserve, in the covering tests, the false-pass guard (real LN routing failure, not the `"refusing to pay"` gate) and trustless recovery (no preimage → SSP claims nothing → user recovers the full coin + intact ladder), present in sdk68 (exact) and sdk66 (non-exact). Do not attempt to preserve the "early-reclaim-blocked-before-batch_timeout" assertion — that SE batch-lock is genuinely absent by design under TES-R local reclaim.

**SSP pre-pay value gate (sdk20, sdk37).** Refuse on both vectors: coin not addressed to the SSP (wrong-recipient theft) and coin worth < invoice+fee (operator loss), with no LN payment emitted and the invoice unsettled. Keep the audit-[3] observed-true-value pin: gate must read the real cryptographically-bound value (V2: `verify_conveyed_child`→`cb.child_state.out_value`, gated by `ladder_census_ok`), never an envelope hint or inflated un-broadcast branch leaf, and must fail **closed**. Keep literal 10000/25000 numeric checks; replacing sdk37's `branch_txs` assert with *nothing* rather than `ladder_census_ok` would silently delete the anti-inflation guarantee.

**Remote-transport trustlessness (sdk21).** Over HTTP: PAY-side `verify_bundle` census (`num_sigs == v1_backups+tiers` from the enclave sig-count) must run before `send_payment`; returned preimage must hash to the invoice hash; RECEIVE-side HODL coordinated clock keeps coin-release a precondition of claiming the HTLC; the 240s client timeout must stay strictly greater than the server worst case (review H1) so a real success is never misread as failure and unsafely reclaimed.

**Re-anchor invalidation (sdk30).** The re-anchor must spend the OLD coin's funding outpoint and mark it WITHDRAWN, permanently invalidating every prior owner's backup/exit (double-spend of a spent input). No other V2 test covers this — do not drop it. If the laddered-root re-anchor path does not work cooperatively, escalate to port-feature rather than weakening the assertion.

**Tokens over time (sdk32).** Two soundness properties: (1) tokens never lost by inactivity (issued and received) — strengthened under V2 (idle coins never age); keep post-idle `token_balance` checks. (2) A received-token holder cannot be clawed back — invert the old "clawback possible" into a positive "sender cannot re-spend/sweep the shared root" assertion (issued carrier terminal-frozen: un-laddered + spend-budget=1), do not silently delete it. Keep the `is_token_carrier` plain-exit guard (a plain unilateral exit must never destroy an RGB allocation).

**Derived-token guards (sdk36).** sdk36 is the sole coverage of: d4 garbage-auth→401, d5 single-use nonce replay refused (audit-[15]), d6 non-owner sig refused, d2 per-request bound, d3 per-parent lifetime cap, and the sentinel pool-isolation invariant that free split/refresh/in-ladder flows never consume paid onboarding tokens. All must survive — this is why it is a rewrite, not a retire.

**Clawback / watchtower retirements (sdk13, sdk14, sdk35).** A stale/prior-owner state must never claw back a coin whose funding F the honest current owner's state already spent, and the honest receiver must always win a contested exit — preserved on V2 by lowest-CSV-current-state-wins (sdk51), stale-ladder-can-never-confirm (sdk40 PART2), unilateral exit (sdk50), rival co-sign rejection (sdk58 H/I), and the R′ receiver census `verify_bundle` + `validate_backup_chain_v2` INV-5 (sdk46/47/54). For sdk35 specifically, back-fill the no-key-material bundle check and the idempotent second `watch_pass` into sdk45/sdk51 **before** deletion, and keep the sender→receiver-trust-NONE property (receiver never books a coin whose ladder is already raceable by a prior owner). Do not delete any of these tests until every named covering test is confirmed green.

**Never-brick guarantee (sdk33 retire).** Passage of time must never render a coin un-spendable/un-transferable and must never force manual ladder management. Under V2 this holds structurally (relative CSV on an un-broadcast trigger) plus unbounded off-chain rollover (sdk43). Do not delete sdk33 or the `auto_refresh` code until sdk43's off-chain-forever renew+rollover+exit and sdk59's split-requiring-transfer paths are confirmed green.

**Asset conservation (sdk23).** Preserve the colored-HTLC checks: A's `offchain_outbound` drops by ≥250 AND B's rises by ≥250 (proving B received, not just that A was debited), plus decode correctness (exact `asset_id`/amount). The migration only strips an inert env pin, so nothing here is at risk — but keep the asserts verbatim.
